PARTLY REPAIRED, pass 43, and still FAIL because ONE payload type inhabits the new primitive and none of the reviewer's four named examples exists in this build at all. WHAT NOW EXISTS. (1) THE PRIMITIVE: interface/contracts/wall_envelope.py::WallNotification, the wall's THIRD shape, carrying NO correlation_id (there is no request to correlate to -- minting a synthetic one is the reviewer's named fail verbatim) and NO status (a status answers a question, and nobody asked), with a MANDATORY payload -- an unsolicited message that says nothing is not a message. Each is refused at construction, not documented. (2) THE ORDERING RULE, which is what the type earns its keep for: `sender` + `sequence` is a position in ONE counterparty's stream, and it makes detectable the single question no amount of reading the messages that DID arrive can answer -- what never came. `notification_id` is separately the C-S2 idempotency key for at-least-once delivery. (3) THE WORLD-SIDE WRITER, which had never existed: simulation/payment_seam_adapter.py::MandateNotificationStream emits ADDACS advices. Before it, `AddacsAdvice` was a payload the contract declared, the company had a reader for (`_observe_addacs`, feeding mandate belief) and NO MODULE ANYWHERE SENT -- a reader with no writer, deliverable only as a WallResponse on a `CollectionRequest` id that is still constructed nowhere but its own contract test. (4) THE CONSUMER RULES: `PaymentObservationConsumer.observe_unsolicited` dedups per (sender, notification_id), counts out-of-order arrival SEPARATELY from loss (a real feed redelivers late far more often than it loses, so one counter mixing them would read as loss every time the transport behaved), and publishes `inbound_stream(sender)` whose `missing_sequences` recomputes from the observed set so a straggler closes a gap without anything having to un-count it. (5) IT IS NOT DARK: wired into background/live_payment_triad.py, the run the company actually drives -- 37 advices crossed in the 150-customer/6-month population, sender BACS-BUREAU-01, and both the company and the D8 shadow are told, for the reason both are billed. WHAT IT DID NOT BUY, MEASURED RATHER THAN HEDGED, and this is the honest headline. EVERY PUBLISHED FIGURE IS BIT-IDENTICAL with and without this leg (detection 0.1181818182, detection_latency 2.135447, belief 0.1470588235, belief_population_mix 0.2666666667, ageing 0.2469740634), and the mandate beliefs are 28 likely_dead_believed either way -- because the ARUDD line ALREADY reported the same mandate fact through the response leg. So this pass bought STRUCTURE and one new DETECTABLE (a missing advice), not a moved belief. Recording it as a capability gain would be the ceremony this walk exists to stop. WHY STILL FAIL, four reasons, none cosmetic. (a) THE REVIEWER'S OWN EXAMPLES ARE ABSENT: pushed D0010s, CSS notifications, DCC alerts and AQ updates are not modelled anywhere in this build, so the primitive is right and the industry flows it was asked about are still missing. (b) THE TRIGGER CAN ONLY FIRE ALONGSIDE A FAILED COLLECTION. `PaymentEvent` is per-payment-attempt and the generator draws no mandate-lifecycle event independent of one, so an advice with NO collection behind it -- the purest unsolicited case, the payer cancelling between collections -- cannot be emitted. Adding that event is a baseline change and is the director's under R13, so it is named, not taken. (c) THE NOTIFICATION LEG DOES NOT TRAVEL THE WIRE: it is at parity with the object-level `observe()` and does NOT pass `decode_framed_response`, so an unsolicited message is accepted from anybody. That is Q13's axis (two of three crossings still unframed) and is the next item on this leg. (d) THE REQUEST LEG IS STILL DORMANT, which is the other half of this question: `tools.wall_channel_census.seam_conversation_conformance` still reads 1 of 3 conversant, correctly, because `CollectionRequest` is constructed nowhere. That is also what keeps Q5(a) -- initial silence being invisible -- unrepaired here. THE INSTRUMENT GAP, filed rather than fixed. The census's leg model is REQUEST/RESPONSE only, so it structurally cannot see a notification leg: it cannot tell 'unsolicited inbound handled by its own primitive' from 'unsolicited inbound faked as a response to nothing', which is exactly the distinction this pass turns on. Its reading is therefore unchanged by design, and a lane that wanted to could green Q2 without the census ever moving. Not fixed in the tick that would benefit from it, and not while a shared 3,504-line module has a suite in flight. A NAMED LIMIT OF THE DETECTOR ITSELF: `missing_sequences` is INTERIOR-ONLY, counted between the lowest and highest sequence seen, because a company that joins a feed at 40 has not lost 0-39. The cost is stated in the type's own docstring -- a notification lost BEFORE the first one ever seen is undetectable and no reading will ever show it. R15, 30 tests added across three files, both directions. MUTATION: test_MUTATION_the_shipped_shape_CANNOT_SEE_the_loss reproduces the pre-repair shape inline (the same advices delivered as WallResponses on synthetic correlation ids), loses two of four, and asserts the loss is INVISIBLE -- the mandates stay merely unheard-of and no reading discloses anything is owed -- beside the new path knowing exactly which two are missing. NULL CONTROLS: a complete stream reports NO gap (so the detector is not always-red); INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS emits no advice and burns no sequence (so the advice is not a duplicate of the ARUDD line); sequence 0 is legal (a `if not sequence` guard would reject the first message of every stream). ORDER-INDEPENDENCE: two arrival orders reach the same belief, so the sequence tells the company what is MISSING and never what is TRUE. Also proven: per-sender id scoping, two senders not sharing a numbering, a redelivery not inflating the stream, a payload the seam does not declare unsolicited being REFUSED, a misdirected advice going to suspense WITHOUT opening a gap, and the source never skipping (without which loss and normality are indistinguishable and the detector measures the fixture).
